controls.name: mode
controls.doc: cut runs the planted bands on the audio; report keeps the audio bit-exact while the detector and the placement run and the report carries what cut would plant. It comes up at cut: a host with no controller gets the corrector. The integer the shell reads is the id's position.

controls.name: pool
controls.doc: Which pool the finds go to: fixed (ring-out: a true notch that never lifts) or live (a rampable bell with the staged release). The integer the shell reads is the id's position, OmxFbsPool's.

controls.name: hold
controls.doc: The clean hold, in seconds, before a live band's first release stage.

controls.name: bands
controls.doc: How many bands this corrector may plant at once (its pool), from one to the EQ's band count. An integer control.

controls.name: merge
controls.doc: The merge radius, in cents. An integer control.

controls.name: cooldown
controls.doc: How long a released find's escalation is remembered, in seconds. An integer control.

SUBHARMONIC_RADIUS_BINS.doc: How far (bins) around bin/2 and bin/3 PSHR (`omx_fbs_pshr`) scans for a sub-harmonic line. A true half/third partial lands mid-bin in the worst case (bin/2 and bin/3 are rarely integers) and spectral leakage smears it one bin further; ±2 covers both. Measured on the #116 live-music corpus: every false positive's sub-line sat inside this window. Deliberately NOT wider — at low bins the window is already a large fraction of an octave, and widening it would start reading unrelated program lines as "sub-harmonics" of real feedback.

FBS_PAPR_GUARD_BINS.doc: PAPR's guard band: bins either side of the peak left out of the floor average (its own skirt).

FBS_PNPR_RADIUS_BINS.doc: PNPR's neighbourhood radius in bins, and the guard inside it that belongs to the peak's own skirt: a pure tone is compared with bins 2 and 3 away on each side.

FBS_PNPR_GUARD_BINS.doc: The guard inside PNPR's neighbourhood radius that belongs to the peak's own skirt, in bins.

FBS_PHPR_HARMONICS.doc: How many harmonics PHPR reads above the candidate: 2f, 3f and 4f.

FBS_PSHR_SELF_SKIP_BINS.doc: PSHR skips sub-window bins within this many of the candidate, so a low bin never measures its own skirt as a sub-harmonic.

FBS_FLOOR_LIN.doc: The magnitude floor of every detector dB reading (−240 dB): a zero bin stays finite.

FBS_TRACK_SLOTS.doc: Tracked candidate bins per armed channel. A candidate that finds no free slot is COUNTED and reported, never dropped silently; the identity corpus peaks at 34.

PSHR_MIN_DB.doc: Minimum PSHR (`omx_fbs_pshr`) (dB) for a candidate frame to count as sub-harmonic-CLEAN. Evidence-set on the #116 corpus, margin on both sides: the four live false positives (musical overtones at 1 869.1 / 832.0 / 263.7 / 228.5 Hz) read PSHR between −10.2 and +8.8 dB across their windows — never a 5-frame sub-clean stretch, and the single closest approach (+8.8) is isolated between frames at ≈ −1 and −10 — while the committed #106 injected ramp reads ≥ +12.2 dB from its second frame on (its frame 0 sits at +9.4, costing exactly one frame of confirm latency, pinned in the corpus test). A static program line at f/2 of REAL feedback also clears this fast: the runaway gains several dB per hop on anything static, so the deferral is transient.

GROWTH_WINDOW_FRAMES.doc: How many of a candidate bin's most recent dB readings feed the growth-slope estimate (the engine's least-squares slope) — set equal to DEFAULT_THRESHOLDS's `persistFrames` so growth is judged over the SAME window persistence already demands (the full run since the bin became a candidate, not a shorter or longer slice of it). Long enough that a couple of noisy/vibrato frames can't fake a trend by themselves.

DEEP_PLATEAU_FRAMES.doc: The DEEP plateau tier's dwell: ~2 s at the watcher's 10 Hz — the TIME that buys the deeper floor its music safety (see DetectThresholds.deepPlateauFloorDb).

GROWTH_MIN_DB_PER_FRAME.doc: Minimum least-squares slope, in dB PER FRAME, over GROWTH_WINDOW_FRAMES for a bin to count as "running away" rather than merely holding level. Set with real margin on BOTH sides — comfortably above measurement jitter on a held tone or a quiet/broadband mix (well under 0.2 dB/frame in practice) and comfortably below a genuine feedback ramp, which climbs several dB across a handful of ~20 ms hops as it heads toward clipping. The acceptance bar is "arming must never burst-alarm on non-growing content", so this errs conservative (under-fire a marginal ramp) rather than tight (risk a false alarm) — the ramp gate (`omx_fbs_is_growing`) also requires the window's end to sit above its start, a cheap belt-and-braces check against a fit dragged positive by one mid-window wobble.

GROWTH_MAX_DIP_DB.doc: Largest single-frame DIP (dB) a run-away window may contain. Real feedback climbs every hop; a small allowance covers measurement jitter and the −0.3 dB-ish wobble frames seen on live captures, while any real drop (a note ending, tremolo) breaks the run.

GROWTH_MIN_TOTAL_RISE_DB.doc: Minimum END-TO-END rise (dB) across the window. The live-music corpus showed sustained melody notes drifting up ~4–5 dB over a window without ever being feedback; a loop past unity gains several dB per hop and clears 6 dB in a window trivially. Below this the tone is holding level, not running away.

GROWTH_MAX_SINGLE_FRAME_SHARE.doc: Cap on the share of the window's total rise a SINGLE frame may carry. Feedback is exponential in amplitude ⇒ linear in dB ⇒ its rise is distributed roughly evenly across the window; a musical attack / re-articulation puts almost the whole rise in one hop (the exact shape behind every one of the 72 live false positives of the live-music corpus). One half is generous to real ramps (an even N-frame ramp puts 1/(N−1) per hop) and fatal to steps. A side effect worth knowing: a 2-sample window can never pass (one hop IS the whole rise), so confirmation always rests on at least three frames of actual ramp evidence.

GROWTH_CONFIRM_FRAMES.doc: How many CONSECUTIVE frames the ramp gate (`omx_fbs_is_growing`) must hold before a bin confirms — the time-domain tiebreak for the one shape a single window cannot judge: a smooth musical crescendo. Within one window a +6 dB swell (live corpus: a C6 at 1 049 Hz, `[-53.7, -51.4, -50.4, -48, -47.3]`) is indistinguishable from slow feedback — the difference is only visible on the NEXT hop, where a crescendo peaks and plateaus (the window's rise collapses) while feedback keeps climbing. Requiring the gate to hold twice in a row costs a clean ramp nothing — its gate is already true while persistence is still arming — and blocks the swell that peaks the very frame it would have confirmed.

DEFAULT_THRESHOLDS.doc: The corpus-tuned SAFE DEFAULT — today's exact gates, assembled byte-for-byte from the exported consts above (which stay the authoritative literal source, so the corpus test's import type { MagnitudeSeries } from './spectrum-bands.js'; imports remain the single truth). This is the ANCHOR the whole sensitivity mapping pins to: thresholdsFor`(0, 'live')` and `(0, 'fixed')` both deep-equal this object, so an untouched channel runs the identical detector it does now. `plateauFloorDb` is omitted ⇒ the #140 plateau route is OFF at the default.

FBS_MAX_NOTCH_DEPTH_DB.doc: THE NOTCH DEPTH LAW: the deepest cut any machine planter may propose from one reading, in dB. A number, not a literal at the call site, because two planters now lean on it. FBS derives a candidate's depth from the peak-to-average ratio around its bin and stops here; Room Analysis derives a mode's depth from its height above the median curve and is held to the SAME ceiling (the room-analysis design — "never more than the FBS notch depth law"). Written twice as `18` those two bounds would be equal by coincidence and could drift apart in silence. It is a CEILING ON THE PROPOSAL, not the final gain: a band that lands as a rampable BELL is bounded again by `EQ_GAIN_RANGE`, which is tighter. A planter must honour both and REPORT when either bit, never quietly deliver a shallower cut than it was asked for.

FBS_DEFAULT_NOTCH_Q.doc: Default planted-notch width (Q) — the dbx-AFS-style ultra-narrow notch the corrector plants. `addBand`'s per-shape clamp holds it at 116 for a fixed notch and narrows it to 8 for a live bell, so this is the declared starting point rather than the width every notch ends up with.

FBS_MAX_CUT_DB.doc: The deepest cut a band of an fbs-* origin may hold, in dB: the feedback corrector's own safety bound, never the operator EQ's ±15 (EQ_GAIN_RANGE), which stays the bound of every other origin. Declared here as one value until the vocabulary owner (omx-contract) carries it as its own word, a new ref beside EQ_GAIN_RANGE and never a widening of it; this item then becomes that ref, and no second copy of the number is ever written.

FBS_RECLAMP_DEEPEN_DB.doc: How much deeper a live band's full depth goes each time regrowth re-clamps a release, in dB, down to FBS_MAX_CUT_DB: regrowth at a depth is the measurement that the depth was not enough.

FBS_RECLAMP_BACKOFF_CAP.doc: The most times the clean hold doubles after re-clamps: the hold before the first release stage is the channel's hold times 2^min(re-clamps, this).

FBS_LIFT_RAMP_MS.doc: How long one release stage's gain ramp takes, in ms, from the depth the band stands at to the stage's depth.

FBS_LIFT_RAMP_STEPS.doc: The equal steps one release ramp takes, FBS_LIFT_RAMP_MS / this apart: the last step lands the stage's depth exactly.

FBS_RELEASE_RATIO.doc: Each release stage holds the planted depth times this ratio to the stage's power: every stage releases a third of what remains.

FBS_RELEASE_DONE_DB.doc: A release stage whose depth is shallower than this, in dB, removes the band instead of holding it: the cut is inaudible.

FBS_RELEASE_DWELL_MS.doc: How long a band listens at an eased stage, clean, before the next stage begins, in ms.

FBS_RING_HZ_MIN.doc: The lowest frequency a confirmed ring is planted at, in Hz; one below it is refused as rejected-edge, never clamped onto the EQ's edge.

FBS_RING_HZ_MAX.doc: The highest frequency a confirmed ring is planted at, in Hz; one above it is refused as rejected-edge.

FBS_SAME_RING_HZ.doc: Two readings are the same ringing frequency within this many Hz, or FBS_SAME_RING_SHARE of the higher one, whichever is wider.

FBS_SAME_RING_SHARE.doc: The share of the higher frequency within which two readings are the same ringing frequency, when it is wider than FBS_SAME_RING_HZ: FFT bin spacing grows with frequency.

FBS_DEFAULT_HOLD_SECONDS.doc: The clean hold, in seconds, before a live band's first release stage.

FBS_DEFAULT_MAX_AUTO_BANDS.doc: How many bands one corrector may plant when nobody set its cap; a full pool plants nothing and says pool-full.

FBS_DEFAULT_MERGE_CENTS.doc: The merge radius, in cents: a confirmed ring this close to a band already planted is that band's find, and plants nothing.

FBS_DEFAULT_COOLDOWN_SECONDS.doc: How long a fully released find's re-clamp count is remembered, in seconds, so a chronic ringer re-plants with its doubled holds.

FBS_WATCH_HZ.doc: The detector's frame rate, in Hz: the cadence the detector gates were tuned at. The live shell's hop is the rate over this.

FBS_RING_MEMORY_SLOTS.doc: Released finds the ring memory holds at once. The console's list is unbounded and expires by FBS_DEFAULT_COOLDOWN_SECONDS; a full memory here forgets its oldest entry first, and counts it.

FBS_MIN_AUTO_BANDS.doc: The smallest pool a corrector may be given: one band. A pool of none is no corrector; the cap is held at or above this.
